title: Test imputed variants for association

blocks.what_we_do: Test the imputed variants of the region around locus L4 for association, with the model of the main analysis. Then compare the simulated risk variant of L4 with the best variant of the region.
blocks.why:
PLINK 2 reads dosages directly from the VCF files that Minimac4 or a server returns. We use the same samples, covariates and principal components as in the main analysis (step 6.4). Otherwise the results of the two analyses cannot be compared. A test on the dosage keeps the uncertainty of each genotype ([Marchini and Howie 2010](https://doi.org/10.1038/nrg2796)).

Locus L4 is a simulated risk variant on chromosome 18 (`chr18:38042715:G:A`, odds ratio 1.4 by design). It is not on the array. In the main analysis the region did not reach genome-wide significance. Does imputation help?

This is one example, from one simulated region and one panel. It shows what can happen. It is not a rule: in another region, or with a larger panel, the result can go either way.
blocks.you_need: Your final cohort from 5.7, the covariates from 6.3 and the imputed output of chromosome 18 in the module A data.
blocks.command:
```{r sA-9}
# 1. Test the imputed dosages of chromosome 18 with the model of the main analysis.
module_a <- file.path(cfg$data_dir, "module_a")
assoc <- imputation_association(cfg, file.path(module_a, "imputed", "chr18.dose.vcf.gz"))
# 2. Check the number of tested variants.
stopifnot(nrow(assoc) == 8334L)
# 3. Compare the L4 variant with the best variant of the region.
print(imputation_l4(assoc))
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --vcf data/course/module_a/imputed/chr18.dose.vcf.gz dosage=DS --double-id --extract-if-info "R2 >= 0.3" --update-sex results/guided/s5-7_state.psam col-num=3 --pheno results/guided/s5-7_state.psam --pheno-name Disease --maf 0.01 --covar results/guided/s6-3_covariates.tsv --covar-name Age,PC1-PC10 --covar-variance-standardize --glm sex hide-covar firth-fallback cols=+a1freq,+machr2 --out results/guided/sA-9_chr18_assoc --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--vcf` reads the imputed output; `dosage=DS` reads the dosage field, and without it PLINK would use the best-guess genotypes in GT. `--double-id` uses the sample name of the VCF as both family ID and individual ID: the course covariate file has the family ID equal to the individual ID, so the rows match. `--extract-if-info "R2 >= 0.3"` keeps the variants whose INFO field R2 is at least 0.3; keep the quotes. A VCF has no sex and no phenotype: `--update-sex` with `col-num=3` takes the sex from column 3 of the sample file of step 5.7. `--pheno` reads the case-control status from the same file, and `--pheno-name Disease` selects its column. `--maf 0.01` keeps variants with a minor allele frequency of at least 1%. `--covar` loads the covariate table, which is keyed by sample ID. `--covar-name` selects Age and PC1 to PC10. `--covar-variance-standardize` rescales the numerical covariates so that the fit is stable. `--glm sex hide-covar firth-fallback` is the model of the main analysis; `cols=+a1freq,+machr2` adds the allele frequency and the r² that PLINK computes from the dosages, a check on the R2 of Minimac4. `--out` sets the prefix of the report files. `--threads 2` limits PLINK to two worker threads. `--memory 2048` gives PLINK 2048 MiB (about 2 GB) of working memory.
blocks.expected_result:
8,334 variants tested. The L4 variant chr18:38042715:G:A: imputation R2 0.95, odds ratio 1.47, p-value 1.7e-06.

| Analysis | Variant | Frequency | R2 | Odds ratio | p-value |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Array sites (main analysis) | best: `18:38107932:C:A`, 65 kb away | 0.25 | measured | 1.49 | 6.6e-07 |
| Imputed | the L4 variant itself | 0.28 | 0.95 | 1.47 | 1.7e-06 |
| Imputed | best in the region: `chr18:38106879:G:C` | 0.41 | 0.81 | 1.54 | 4.2e-08 |
| True genotypes (only in a simulation) | the L4 variant | 0.29 | | 1.46 | 1.3e-06 |
| True genotypes (only in a simulation) | best in the region | 0.37 | | 1.46 | 1.6e-07 |

The rows of the array sites and of the true genotypes come from the author's run, not from this chunk.

What this example shows:

- The L4 variant is imputed well. Its result is almost the same as with its true genotype.
- It is not the top of its region. Variants 50 to 80 kb away, in LD with it, give smaller p-values. This happens in real studies too: the lead variant is not necessarily the cause (step 7.6).
- After imputation the best variant crosses 5e-08. With the true genotypes, the region does not go below 1.6e-07. Here, part of the "genome-wide significant" result comes from noise in the dosages of a variant with R2 0.81. Noise can push a p-value up as well as down; in this region it pushed it down.


Validation: executable chunks passed on Windows with PLINK 2.0 b.1.4 on the 1,811 samples of the course cohort (data release 2026.1) and the module A data. The numbers equal the run of the author on 23 November 2026.
blocks.troubleshooting: "The L4 variant is not in the result": the R2 filter or the frequency filter removed it; check the filters. Many samples with missing phenotypes: the dosage file and your cohort come from different data releases. Use the module A data of the same release as your course data. A different number of tested variants: check that you kept the quotes around "R2 >= 0.3".
blocks.quick_check:
After imputation, a variant with R2 0.81 crosses the genome-wide threshold, while the array site next to it does not. Is the imputed result a discovery?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

Not yet. In this example the true genotypes do not reach the threshold: part of the result comes from noise in the dosages. Report the R2 of every variant you discuss, look at the measured neighbours, and confirm by direct genotyping or in another study.

</details>

student_summary: We test the imputed variants of the region around locus L4 for association with disease, with the same model as the main analysis. We compare the result of the simulated risk variant, which is not on the array, with the best variant of the region.

options.name: --vcf
options.explanation: Reads the imputed output of chromosome 18 from the module A data.

modifiers.name: dosage
modifiers.explanation: With DS, reads the dosage field: the expected number of copies of the alternate allele, from 0 to 2.

options.name: --double-id
options.explanation: Uses the sample name of the VCF file as both family ID and individual ID, so that the rows match the covariate file.

options.name: --extract-if-info
options.explanation: Keeps the variants whose imputation quality R2, in the INFO column, is at least 0.3.

options.name: --update-sex
options.explanation: Takes the recorded sex of each sample from s5-7_state.psam, because a VCF file has no sex.

modifiers.name: col-num
modifiers.explanation: With 3, reads the sex from column 3 of that file.

options.name: --pheno
options.explanation: Reads the case and control status from s5-7_state.psam, because a VCF file has no phenotype.

options.name: --pheno-name
options.explanation: Selects the column Disease of that file.

options.name: --maf
options.explanation: Keeps variants whose less common allele (DNA version) has a frequency of at least 1% in the study group.

options.name: --covar
options.explanation: Reads s6-3_covariates.tsv, matching age and genetic component scores to samples by their IDs.

options.name: --covar-name
options.explanation: Selects Age and PC1 to PC10 as extra factors to adjust the disease comparison; each PC describes one pattern of genetic variation.

options.name: --covar-variance-standardize
options.explanation: Rescales the numerical adjustment factors to mean zero and variance one, a common scale that helps the model calculation remain stable.

options.name: --glm
options.explanation: Fits a logistic model at each variant to estimate how each extra copy of the tested DNA version changes the odds of disease.

modifiers.name: sex
modifiers.explanation: Adds the recorded sex as an adjustment factor in the model.

modifiers.name: hide-covar
modifiers.explanation: Reports the genetic tests without separate rows for the effects of age, sex and genetic component scores.

modifiers.name: firth-fallback
modifiers.explanation: Uses Firth correction, which gives usable estimates when very few people carry the allele, when the ordinary model calculation fails.

modifiers.name: cols
modifiers.explanation: With +a1freq,+machr2, adds the allele frequency and the imputation quality that PLINK computes from the dosages.

options.name: --out
options.explanation: Starts output file names with sA-9_chr18_assoc, including sA-9_chr18_assoc.Disease.glm.logistic.hybrid.
